children: Slovakia's annual inflation rate eased to 3.1% in August 2026 from 3.3% in July, slightly below market expectations of 3.2%.
This marked the lowest reading since December 2024, largely due to a deeper decline in food and non-alcoholic beverage prices (-2.5% vs -2.1%).

Inflation also slowed for clothing and footwear (0.4% vs 0.8%), furnishings, household equipment and routine household maintenance (1.3% vs 1.4%), health (4.8% vs 5.1%), transport (6.5% vs 7.0%), recreation, sport and culture (4.7% vs 5.2%), education (5.9% vs 6.0%), and insurance and financial services (4.5% vs 4.6%).
Meanwhile, price growth accelerated for alcoholic beverages, tobacco and narcotics (2.6% vs 1.8%) and information and communication (2.3% vs 2.2%).
On a monthly basis, consumer prices were unchanged, in line with market expectations and compared with a 0.1% increase in July.
Core inflation, which excludes regulated prices, edged down to 1.5% from 1.7% in July, marking its lowest level since February 2021.

title: Slovakia Inflation Lowest Since 2024
